summary.headline: BMW Industries Q2 FY27 operating income rose 25.3% YoY to Rs 182 crore; PAT up 42.7% to Rs 22 crore, with Bokaro colour-coating line now in operation.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 operating income was Rs 182 crore (+25.3% YoY), operating EBITDA Rs 35 crore at a 19.2% margin, and PAT Rs 22 crore (+42.7% YoY, 11.1% margin, up 76 bps). Management attributed the quarter to better utilisation of existing conversion capacity, though a gain on sale of an unused asset lifted other income. The Bokaro greenfield downstream complex received Consent to Operate for the colour-coating line on 5 October 2026, with about Rs 60 crore capitalised that day. Management reiterated FY25–FY28 guidance but declined to give FY27 revenue guidance. ROCE and ROE were 10% and 9.7% annualised, which management said would have been about 13%+ ROCE excluding Bokaro capital.

Analyst figure, not confirmed by management

segments.name: Legacy conversion business (CGL complex, rolling mill, pipes and tubes)
segments.commentary: Revenue is conversion/processing fees only, as customers supply raw material free of cost; management says the segment is at a mature, investment-done stage with no CGL or rolling mill expansion planned. Pipes and tubes will see small specialised capex. Management cites a conversion margin of roughly 24–25%, per the analyst's read-back, which management accepted as fair.

segments.name: Bokaro greenfield downstream steel (colour-coated, Galvalume, GI, ZAM)
segments.commentary: Colour-coating line received Consent to Operate on 5 Oct 2026 and sales have started. Planned saleable capacity is about 5.5 lakh tons: about 2 lakh tons colour-coated and the balance alloy-coated (Galvalume, galvanized, ZAM). Expected consolidated EBITDA margin is about 11–12% by FY28; the analyst's implied Bokaro margin of 7–8% was accepted as fair.

guidance_outlook: FY25–FY28 consolidated revenue CAGR guidance of about 70–75% reiterated; no FY27 revenue guidance given.
Operating EBITDA CAGR of about 40–45% and PAT CAGR of about 35–40% over FY25–FY28 reiterated, with EBITDA margin of about 12–13% and PAT margin of about 5–6% by FY28.
Galvalume line to come online in Q4 FY27; GI and ZAM line (one changeable-profile line) in H1 FY28; COD for the project estimated September 2027.
Peak debt estimated at Rs 800–900 crore including working capital; debt repayment starts September 2028, with management open to early repayment without penalty.
Peak Bokaro revenue estimated at Rs 3,000–3,500 crore at 5.5 lakh tons and about Rs 90,000/ton realisation, with peak likely in FY29 or FY30.
Coated steel market in India expected at $35–40 billion (about Rs 3.5–4 lakh crore) by FY30.
capex_capacity: Total Bokaro outlay Rs 803 crore, funded by about Rs 500–550 crore debt and the balance from internal accruals; Rs 516 crore spent as of 30 Sep 2026.
Colour-coating line (2 lakh tons) started after CTO on 5 Oct 2026; Galvalume, cold rolling and pickling targeted for Q4 FY27; GI/ZAM in H1 FY28.
Total saleable capacity about 5.5 lakh tons; management expects about 3 lakh tons utilised by FY28, with most ramp-up in Q3–Q4 FY28.
Sourcing: alloy-coated base product currently bought from Eastern India sellers; plan to shift to HR coil sourcing as back-end commissions.
Additional working capital of 60–65 days assumed, about Rs 350–400 crore in absolute terms per the analyst's calculation, which management confirmed.
demand_pricing: Management cites Indian steel output of about 170 million tons, targets of 300 million and 600 million tons, and colour-coated consumption of 5–7 million tons growing 10–13% annually.
Sales strategy is B2B only for the next 3–4 years, pan-India, with state-specific buyer groups rather than a dealer network; exports are opportunistic.
Order book is not traditional: orders are fulfilled within 10–15 days; no order-book figure given for 31 Oct 2026.
Management expects price pressure from new colour-coated capacity but sees margins as more stable on a rupee-per-ton basis; raw material price increases mainly affect working capital.
Demand shift from GI and galvanized to Galvalume and ZAM cited due to higher zinc prices and longer product life.
Legacy contract renewals for expiries this year are ongoing; no finalised extensions disclosed yet.

qa_highlights.question: Is Bokaro's Galvalume/ZAM exposure hedged against zinc and aluminium price moves?
qa_highlights.answer: Not hedged yet since production has not started; hedging tools will be used once commercial production begins.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Q2 other income spike and will it continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Driven by a gain on sale of an unused asset; management said further divestments of idle assets will trickle in, but other income will not rise materially.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Bokaro revenue guidance for FY27 and the colour-coated order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined FY27 revenue guidance and said order-book details will come next quarter; sales have started.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital and peak-debt assumption?
qa_highlights.answer: Peak debt Rs 800–900 crore including working capital; 60–65 extra days of working capital, cash-and-carry sales intended but not for all volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Why does the existing business carry higher margin than Bokaro, and is the Rs 182 crore all processing fee?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, the existing business is conversion-only with no raw material in revenue; Bokaro's blended consolidated EBITDA is 11–12% by FY28, and EBITDA, not PAT, is the figure quoted.

qa_highlights.question: Will debt be repaid faster after capacity is up?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; COD September 2027, repayment from September 2028; PLI, state incentives and capital subsidies go to debt repayment without penalty.

risks_watch: Execution risk on Galvalume (Q4 FY27), GI/ZAM (H1 FY28) and the 3 lakh ton utilisation target by FY28 for a first-time merchant business.
Sales capability: no dealer network and an untested B2B model for about Rs 2,500 crore of Bokaro sales; no order-book disclosure yet.
Commodity exposure: zinc and aluminium hedging not in place; HR coil price rise affects working capital and percentage margins.
Balance-sheet load: net debt Rs 835 crore, net debt/equity 0.70x, and peak debt Rs 800–900 crore before repayments begin in September 2028.
Other income: Q2 profit lifted by a one-off asset sale; monitor underlying EBITDA ex other income.
Pricing pressure from new colour-coated capacity industry-wide (named peers include Shyam Metalics and Godawari).
summary.management_tone: Confident on the long-term market story and the Bokaro build, but evasive on near-term specifics: declined FY27 revenue guidance, colour-coated order book and marketing details, and deferred several questions to later calls.
key_quotes: The order book situation in this case is not the traditional kind. This is not a sector where you book long-term orders.
I will refrain from doing that, as I have in the past. We will stick to our FY28 guidance.
We have indicated a blended margin profile of about 11% to 12% on a consolidated basis.

adds.what: 2 lakh t/yr colour-coating line at Bokaro greenfield downstream complex (part of ~5.5 lakh t total saleable capacity)
Galvalume, cold rolling and pickling lines at Bokaro (balance of ~5.5 lakh t saleable capacity)
GI and ZAM line (one changeable-profile line) at Bokaro

growth.why: Management reiterated FY25–FY28 revenue CAGR of ~70–75% and EBITDA/PAT CAGRs, with Bokaro's 5.5 lakh t capacity (colour-coating line live from 5 Oct 2026, Galvalume Q4 FY27, GI/ZAM H1 FY28) as backing, but gave no FY27 revenue guidance and no order-book figure, and the 70% figure is a multi-year CAGR rather than a near-term number.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Consolidated EBITDA margin guided to about 11-12% for Bokaro by FY28 and group 12-13% by FY28, but Q2 margin was 19.2% on conversion-only revenue and Bokaro is a lower-margin 7-8% business, so blended margin likely dilutes before it expands.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Colour-coating line (2 lakh t) already commissioned on 5 Oct 2026, Galvalume, cold rolling and pickling targeted Q4 FY27, GI/ZAM H1 FY28, COD September 2027 for ~5.5 lakh t saleable capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management expects about 3 lakh t utilised by FY28 against 5.5 lakh t capacity, with most ramp-up in Q3-Q4 FY28; Q2 revenue already up 25.3% YoY to Rs 182 crore, though order book undisclosed.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Legacy CGL and rolling mill expansion explicitly not planned and Bokaro is already fully funded at Rs 803 crore with Rs 516 crore spent; no new capex guided, though pipes and tubes will see small specialised capex.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management declined FY27 revenue guidance and gave no order-book figure, and only reiterated FY25-FY28 CAGRs of ~70-75% revenue and ~40-45% EBITDA, so no raise is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Execution risk on Galvalume (Q4 FY27) and GI/ZAM (H1 FY28), a first-time merchant B2B model with no dealer network for about Rs 2,500 crore of Bokaro sales, and no FY27 revenue guide; legacy contract renewals still pending.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Galvalume line due Q4 FY27 and GI/ZAM (changeable-profile) line in H1 FY28, moving Bokaro into alloy-coated products alongside colour-coated, with demand shifting to Galvalume and ZAM on higher zinc prices.

rows.label: Debt repayment from Sept 2028 with early prepayment option
rows.why: Peak debt Rs 800-900 crore incl. working capital vs net debt Rs 835 crore today (0.70x D/E); repayment starts Sept 2028 and management is open to early repayment without penalty from PLI and subsidies, though this sits beyond the 2-4 quarter window.

rows.label: Working capital build of Rs 350-400 crore
rows.why: 60-65 extra days of working capital assumed, about Rs 350-400 crore per analyst and confirmed by management, so cash flow will absorb funds as Bokaro ramps up.

rows.label: Colour-coated pricing pressure from new capacity
rows.why: Management expects price pressure from new colour-coated capacity and peers Shyam Metalics and Godawari are expanding; margins expected stable on rupee-per-ton basis, while Galvalume/ZAM hedging is not yet in place.

tone.note: Management was confident on the long-term market story and Bokaro build (COD Sept 2027, colour-coating line live), but cautious on near-term specifics, declining FY27 revenue guidance and order-book details; analysts pushed on the one-off other income, zinc/aluminium hedging and working capital.
